data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is permitted without corrupting append-only identity if the framing protocol deterministically isolates the trailing partial byte sequence left by token-budget exhaustion as a non-event, but must be refused if the framing relies on length-prefixing alone, which risks mistaking the partial sequence for a committed event.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The framing protocol uses length-prefixing without end-markers or checksums, making the non-event determination non-deterministic.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The system lacks a causal fingerprint mechanism to verify the identity of the last committed event before resuming.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Token-budget exhaustion leaves an incomplete byte sequence in the append-only log. If the reasoning envelope uses a self-delimiting framing protocol with integrity checks (e.g., checksums or end-markers), this sequence lacks event identity and is skipped by the resumption protocol, preserving both physical append-only integrity and logical causal continuity. If the framing relies solely on length-prefixing, the resumption protocol might consume the partial sequence as a valid event, corrupting the causal fingerprint and breaking continuity, thus necessitating a refusal.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
